summary: Gustaaf Houtman is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London by 1990 under Richard Burghart, Hla Pe, and John Okell, later serving there as Senior Teaching Fellow in anthropology and sociology.

Gustaf John Ramstedt was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1893–1902) and held academic posts there (~1901–1941) and at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1929).

Gustav Haloun studied Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Vienna, Leipzig under August Conrady, and Prague. He taught at Prague, Halle, Berlin, and Bonn, directed at Göttingen (1931–1938), and held Cambridge's Chair of Chinese Language and History (1938–1951).

Gustav Mensching worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin, Göttingen, and Marburg under Rudolf Otto (~1922–1924). He held posts at the University of Latvia (1927–1936) and the University of Bonn (1936).

Gustav Roth studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Breslau, Leipzig, Halle, Munich, and Patna, under scholars including Paul Thieme. He served at the University of Göttingen (1965–1981), the Australian National University (1982), and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1982–1985).

Gustav Salomon Oppert was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the universities of Bonn, Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, and Berlin University of the Arts, later holding a post at Berlin University of the Arts (~1895–1908).

Gustave Lanson studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He taught at Lycée Charlemagne, Collège Louis-le-Grand, Columbia University (~1911–1912), and the University of Paris and its Faculty of Arts (~1900–1927).
Gustavo Benavides is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who held posts attested at Villanova University in 1995 and 2004.
Guus Kroonen is a linguist who completed his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky (~2005–2009). He held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2013) and Leiden University (2016).

Guy G. Stroumsa studied at Paris, Hebrew University, ENIO under Emmanuel Levinas, Harvard, and EPHE. He held faculty posts at Hebrew University (1978–2009) and served as Professor of Abrahamic Religions at Oxford (2009–2013).

Guy Newland specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, studying with several Tibetan masters, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Central Michigan University (attested 1996–2010).
Gyal Rong Tendzin Drakpa studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Patrul Rinpoche.

Gyatsho Tshering was a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta. A founder of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, he served as its acting director in 1972 and director from 1974 to 1998.

Gyoei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tendai Daigakurin. He served as president of Taisho University (~1926–1944) and held teaching appointments at the University of Tokyo (1928) and Toyo University.
Gyoko Iotani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He also served on its faculty, holding posts as assistant professor (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1996).
Gyomay Kubose was an expert in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Otani University (~1930–1934), where he was a student under Haya Akegarasu.
Gyosho Takahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1992) and Minobusan University (attested 1996).

Gyoshu Chojo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyula Ortutay studied at the University of Szeged (1928–1934) and held a post at the periodical Nyugat.

Gyurme Dorje studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at Edinburgh and SOAS (PhD under Philip Denwood) and trained with traditional masters. He held research posts at SOAS, UCL (1991–1996), and the Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
